name: Gray Matter
label: Dischord
lede: Four friends from junior high walked out of a skinhead-shadowed band, made hardcore sing, broke up for college, came back, and then one of them built the room where DC still goes to see shows.

eras.title: Walking out of Iron Cross
eras.text: Gray Matter started as an exit. Dante Ferrando and Mark Haggerty quit Iron Cross when, as Dischord puts it, the band's image began to reflect its violent supporters more than its members, and they went back to the friends they'd been playing with since junior high.

years.h: Dante Ferrando and Mark Haggerty quit [[Iron Cross|13afe528-54f1-4955-bbec-a4bafb590edb]]
years.p: Drummer [[Dante Ferrando|98b1e2a2-3868-47f0-b905-35637b5a902f]] and guitarist [[Mark Haggerty|235b9917-3f4c-4670-ade3-d94f8e45a044]] leave Iron Cross, D.C.'s skinhead-favorite band, uneasy with the crowd it was drawing.

years.h: Before Gray Matter, they were the G-men
years.p: Before the name Gray Matter stuck, Geoff Turner, Steve Niles, Mark Haggerty and Dante Ferrando played as G-men. Dischord's history says they'd been making noise together since junior high.

years.h: Gray Matter, officially
years.p: [[Geoff Turner|591fc466-2668-4524-852d-a6cc5f18cff7]] on vocals and guitar, [[Steve Niles|ce17b293-3129-426d-b9d3-7403dfda4d8f]] on bass, Mark Haggerty on guitar, Dante Ferrando on drums. Summer 1983, and all four were still high school kids.
years.xp:
Dischord dates the official start to the summer of 1983. The lineup of Turner, Niles, Haggerty and Ferrando would be the one on every Gray Matter record, across two separate runs.

The University of Maryland's DC punk archive calls them one of the defining acts of the Revolution Summer era: hardcore's drive, with far more melody and craft than 1981 allowed.

eras.title: Hardcore that learned to sing
eras.text: While DC's first wave burned out, Gray Matter wrote songs with hooks and made two records at Inner Ear with Ian MacKaye in the chair. It put them at the center of the melodic turn that people would later file under Revolution Summer and, eventually, post-hardcore.

years.h: Food For Thought comes out on R&B, not Dischord
years.p: Cut at Inner Ear in November 1984 with [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and Bert Queiroz producing, Gray Matter's debut LP lands on R&B Records while the band is still in high school.
years.xp:
MacKaye sang backups on the sessions. "Oscar's Eye" would later be Dischord's pick for its 20th-anniversary box.

Dischord's own page is clear that the album first came out on R&B Records in 1985, and only later joined the Dischord catalog as No. 48. The Wikipedia track list also includes a cover of the Beatles' "I Am the Walrus" from the same November 1984 sessions.

The name has a D.C. echo: Food for Thought was also the Dupont Circle vegetarian restaurant run by Dante Ferrando's father, Bobby, from 1973 to 1999, a room that hosted punk shows. No source we found says the album was named for it.

years.h: Gray Matter's "Walk the Line" on Alive and Kicking
years.p: An early version of "Walk the Line" shows up on Alive and Kicking, the WGNS compilation 7", Gray Matter's first link to the studio Geoff Turner would go on to run.

years.h: Gray Matter back at Inner Ear for a second session
years.p: Six songs with Ian MacKaye producing, including "Chutes and Ladders" and the seven-minute-plus "Head".

years.h: On the roof of Food for Thought during Revolution Summer, 1985
yt: On the roof of Food for Thought during Revolution Summer, 1985

years.h: Take It Back · Dischord No. 21
years.p: The 12" EP puts Gray Matter on Dischord proper. Tight, bright and sung, it's the record fans hand people to explain the band.

years.h: Mark Haggerty leaves for college and Gray Matter splits
years.p: Guitarist Mark Haggerty heads off to school and Gray Matter calls it quits. Drummer Dante Ferrando joins [[Ignition|3cb2b7d6-1f0b-4ac5-b67f-52132f3d3b61]].
years.xp:
Dischord's history says Mark Haggerty left for college shortly after Take It Back and the band broke up. Wikipedia dates the split to May 1986.

Wikipedia also lists a second guitarist, [[Jon Kirschten|660b0e16-ab22-49b4-8646-6777c432da4c]], in the band from 1985 to 1986, who went on to form [[Rain|4e9323df-ca77-4e43-addf-bb520fb1b983]]. Dischord's history doesn't mention him.

eras.title: Three, with a Minor Threat rhythm section
eras.text: The breakup barely slowed anyone down. Three of the four regrouped with Jeff Nelson from Minor Threat, and for a moment Ian MacKaye too, in a band that pushed DC further toward melody.

years.h: Geoff Turner and Steve Niles form Three with MacKaye and Nelson
years.p: Gray Matter's Geoff Turner and Steve Niles join [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and [[Jeff Nelson|51f7994c-949d-4dbe-89eb-2c33f42a5620]]. MacKaye soon leaves, Mark Haggerty steps in on guitar, and Turner ends up singing.

years.h: Three plays its last show at the 9:30 Club
years.p: New Year's Day at D.C.'s 9:30 Club. Three's only album, Dark Days Coming, comes out on Dischord in 1989.

years.h: Live at DC Space, 1989

eras.title: The second run, and a club of their own
eras.text: Gray Matter came back in 1990 as grown men with a studio of their own, Geoff Turner's WGNS, and made their most ambitious record there. When it ended again in 1993, drummer Dante Ferrando opened the Black Cat, the venue that would anchor D.C.'s scene for the next thirty years.

years.h: Gray Matter's original four reform
years.p: Geoff Turner, Steve Niles, Mark Haggerty and Dante Ferrando, the 1983 lineup, are back. Dischord also gathers Food For Thought and Take It Back onto one CD that year, No. 49.

years.h: Gray Matter's 4 Songs, a double seven-inch
years.p: Dischord and WGNS co-release it. Two of the four, "Bite the Bit" and "October", get new versions on Thog.

years.h: Gray Matter splits a 7" with [[Severin|4e4b4490-1c10-4e0c-b794-afa4688f88a6]]
years.p: Gray Matter's "Second Guess" backs Severin on a Dischord/Superbad split 7". Mark Haggerty would join Severin later.

years.h: Thog: Gray Matter's full-length, cut at WGNS
years.p: Eleven songs recorded at Geoff Turner's WGNS Studios and produced by the band. Dischord No. 68, and out of print on CD and LP for years.

years.h: Gray Matter breaks up again
years.p: The second run closes. Geoff Turner keeps producing at WGNS, and Steve Niles is already writing comics.

years.h: [[Dante Ferrando|98b1e2a2-3868-47f0-b905-35637b5a902f]] opens the Black Cat
years.p: The D.C. club's first show is by 9353. Ferrando built the Black Cat with a group of investors that included [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]].
years.xp:
Ferrando named the club after a place his great-grandfather ran in Greenwich Village in the 1920s. Its café served mostly vegetarian food and was named Food for Thought, after his father Bobby's Dupont Circle restaurant.

For DC punk it meant a home. Anniversaries at the Black Cat would become the only reliable way to see Gray Matter again.

eras.title: The house band for birthdays
eras.text: Gray Matter never quite reunited, and never quite went away. Every five years the Black Cat throws itself a party, and the original four show up for it.

years.cap: Gray Matter at the Black Cat
years.h: Gray Matter plays the Black Cat's 10th anniversary
years.p: Billed as a one-off, it turned into a habit: Gray Matter came back for the club's 15th, 20th, 25th and 30th anniversaries too.

years.h: Dischord remasters Gray Matter's early records
years.p: Dischord remasters its Food For Thought/Take It Back CD, No. 49.

years.h: Steve Niles' 30 Days of Night hits theaters
years.p: The film of Gray Matter bassist [[Steve Niles|ce17b293-3129-426d-b9d3-7403dfda4d8f]]'s vampire comic with Ben Templesmith opens. Niles had started out self-publishing through Arcane Comix.

years.h: Reunion at the Black Cat's 15th anniversary, September 12, 2008
yt: Reunion at the Black Cat's 15th anniversary, September 12, 2008

years.h: Gray Matter's early records back on vinyl
years.p: Food For Thought and Take It Back are re-cut on vinyl. Take It Back grows to ten songs, adding the four from the 1991 4 Songs double seven-inch, on blue vinyl.
